items.raw_snippet: ChatGPT maker OpenAI has confidentially filed for a US initial public offering, the company said on Monday, joining rivals such as Anthropic in a race towards public markets amid surging investor interest in artificial intelligence. ChatGPT maker OpenAI confidentially filed for a US initial public offering recently, the company said on Monday, joining rival Anthropic in a push towards the stock market as investors seek exposure to the artificial intelligence boom. OpenAI did not disclose the size or terms of the offering, and said a timeline has not yet been determined. Reuters had reported that the AI giant is targeting a valuation of up to $1 trillion in a stock market debut that could come as early as September. Anthropic, the company behind the viral coding assistant Claude Code, said on June 1 it had confidentially filed for a US initial public offering, weeks after raising $65 billion in a funding round that valued it at $965 billion.

OpenAI is working with Goldman Sachs Group Inc and Morgan Stanley on a potential listing as soon as in the fall, people familiar with the matter have said. OpenAI is also planning to launch a tender sale of its shares to provide liquidity to employees in the coming weeks, before the company goes public, according to a person familiar with the matter. Though the company and its flagship chatbot remain synonymous with AI for many people, OpenAI also faces a number of challenges, including heightened competition from Anthropic PBC and Alphabet Inc’s Google. items.raw_snippet: When AI startup Anthropic confidentially filed for an initial public offering, or IPO, last week, it intensified what many observers have framed as a mad rush to cash in on investor enthusiasm amid one of the most historic market booms the tech sector has ever seen. Following months of what many have described as an historic stock rally driven largely by a surge of investment in companies — such as Nvidia, AMD and Intel — that produce AI parts, a wave of AI IPOs may serve as a reality check for a market largely driven by expectations about the technology’s future potential, experts say. Anthropic joins SpaceX, which filed to go public last month, as two of the three most highly anticipated equity offerings in recent memory, with the third — OpenAI — expected to follow suit in the coming weeks. SpaceX is widely expected to debut at a valuation exceeding $1 trillion, potentially making it the largest IPO in history, while OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s expected valuations appear to be closing in on $1 trillion, respectively.

items.snippet: ###### Software acquisition deals hit lowest level since COVID due to AI. The so...
items.raw_snippet: ###### Software acquisition deals hit lowest level since COVID due to AI. The software sector recorded its lowest value of private equity buyout deals since the onset of the pandemic, as the accelerating development of artificial intelligence forced investors to reassess the sector's future. Data from *PitchBook*, cited by *Financial Times*, points to a decline in the value of software company buyout deals to $50 billion in the first five months of 2026, compared to $88 billion in the same period last year. Until last year, the value of software company buyout deals reached $290 billion, the highest level in 11 years. If the current slowdown continues until the end of the year, 2026 will be the weakest year since 2018 in terms of deal activity in this sector. In May, the value of completed or announced deals dropped to just $5 billion, compared to $29 billion in the same month last year.
